summary: Dashboard KPI tile: label, Intl-formatted value, textual change, icon, a small decorative trend line and a footer slot.
whenToUse: Rows of indicators at the top of an admin dashboard.
Showing the recent trend of a metric next to its current value.
whenNotToUse: Detailed time-series analysis: use LineChart or a table.
Metrics without their own surface inside another card: use Statistic.

props.name: value
props.description: Numbers are formatted with Intl.NumberFormat in the current locale; null shows emptyValue.

props.name: trend
props.description: Change; the direction is announced in localized words. sentiment also colors the trend line.

props.name: sparkline
props.description: Recent values drawn as a decorative SVG line (aria-hidden); non-finite values are ignored, at least 2 points are required.

props.name: footer
props.description: Link to details, a small action or a note.

props.name: variant
props.description: Surface: default (neutral), vivid (brand gradient with primary-foreground text, for the main KPI), tinted (tonal fill).

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Renders a SkeletonKpi of the same shape in its place (aria-busy, hidden non-live “Loading…” text) while keeping className and style, so it stays in the grid. Wrap the area in SkeletonGroup for a single announcement. With sparkline={[]} or icon the placeholder reserves room for the line and the icon.

inherits: HTML attributes of <div> (id, style, data-*, aria-*).
accessibility: Value and change are text: the trend line is aria-hidden and carries no exclusive information.
The trend direction is written out for screen readers (“increase”, “decrease”…), not just an arrow or color.
In forced-colors the line uses CanvasText and the shaded area is hidden; the vivid and tinted variants fall back to Canvas/CanvasText with a border.
The vivid variant uses the brand gradient/foreground pair, designed for contrast at both ends of the gradient.
responsive: Fluid width: use Grid with minItemWidth for KPI rows that wrap.
The trend line adapts to the width while keeping the stroke thickness.
customization: Tokens: --dc-look-radius-container, feedback colors for the trend; vivid uses --dc-gradient-accent, --dc-color-action-primary-foreground and --dc-look-shadow-primary; tinted uses --dc-look-fill-tonal on --dc-color-action-secondary.
In vivid, label, description, trend and trend line inherit the primary-foreground color (currentColor): the sentiment stays readable thanks to the arrow and text.
commonMistakes: Conveying information through the trend line alone: repeat it in the trend or the description.
Formatting numbers by hand and ignoring the locale.
Treating a decrease as negative when it is positive (e.g. errors): set sentiment.
Using vivid on every card in a row: reserve it for the main KPI, otherwise it loses emphasis.

limits: The built-in trend line is deliberately minimal (no axes, tooltip or highlighted point): for explorable charts use Sparkline or LineChart.
The footer is not a clickable area: to make the whole card navigable, place the KpiCard in a structure with an explicit link.
